title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse
summary: The method replaces full prefill of retrieved context with independent chunk-cache reuse plus a small repair budget spent on the answer-bearing chunk, preferentially by recomputing that chunk against the reused cache and placing it next to the question. It costs retriever dependence, extra orchestration to identify and move the target chunk, and workload-specific validation across models and datasets. It can fail when the retriever misses the target, when useful damage is spread across many similar chunks, and on dialogue-memory workloads where token-level selection remains competitive or better.
rationale: For a constrained production team, the paper supports a narrow, low-budget intervention worth A/B testing in retrieval-heavy QA systems, but the benefit is setting-dependent and not reliable enough for blanket adoption.
technique: Targeted KV-cache repair for non-prefix reuse

claims.statement: The method replaces full prefill of retrieved context with independent chunk-cache reuse plus a small repair budget spent on the answer-bearing chunk, preferentially by recomputing that chunk against the reused cache and placing it next to the question. It costs retriever dependence, extra orchestration to identify and move the target chunk, and workload-specific validation across models and datasets. It can fail when the retriever misses the target, when useful damage is spread across many similar chunks, and on dialogue-memory workloads where token-level selection remains competitive or better.

Recomputing the retriever's top chunk after moving it next to the question significantly beats InfoFlow-style reordering at the same 5% budget in six of nine open-domain QA and API-documentation settings; question attention alone selects the answer-bearing chunk in at most 18.8% of development questions.
